source.full: Book Of Online Sourced Triumphs 6: Space Fantasy

gear.name: R94 Arcane Rifle
description: The R94 Arcane Rifle is a magically powered rifle. It uses inlaid spells to propel the bullets. There is a display screen on the rifle which lets the user draw spellwork on the bullet itself, though the bullet's surface area limits what can be accomplished with the spellwork.
Because someone's {@skill Arcana} knowledge can increase the effectiveness of this weapon, it gains the {@quality Arcane Magitek} weapon quality.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

gear.name: Divine Pistol
description: The Divine Pistol is a certain type of pistol with prayers written on the handles. It comes in a number of different makes and models, the main difference between them being which god the prayers are written to. The gods tend to aid the aim of those who follow them.
Because someone's faith can increase the effectiveness of this weapon, it gains the {@quality Divine Magitek} weapon quality.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

gear.name: Lightbow
description: The Lightbow may seem low-tech, but it is a highly innovative invention. It funnels the energy of the user's surroundings into the string of the bow. The tension of the bowstring fluctuates based on the user's need, making it easy to draw the bow while retaining attack power upon release.
The user can use their {@skill Primal} magical capability to increase the bow's attack power.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

gear.name: Artificer's Gear
description: Artificer's gear includes all the tools found in the {@gear artificer's toolkit}, as well as advanced diagnostic tools and an artificial intelligence which helps troubleshoot problems.

While in possession of artificer's gear, you are considered to be in possession of an {@gear artificer's toolkit}. When using artificer's gear, while making an {@skill Artifice|artificing} check, add {@symbols s} to the result.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

gear.name: Artificer's Toolkit
description: The artificer's toolkit provides the tools necessary to build, disassemble, repair, or modify just about anything mechanical or Magitek based. A true artificer would not be caught dead without their toolkit.

The artificer's toolkit is treated as the "{@rule The Right Tool for the Job|right tool for the job}" when making {@skill Artifice|artificing} checks (as well as {@skill mechanics} checks, if your setting is using the {@skill Mechanics} skill).
{@b Author:} Craftidore

gear.name: Primal Radar
description: The primal radar is a wilderness survival tool which links the mind of the user to any surrounding plants and small animals within Medium range. In areas of light vegetation (such as a room with multiple house plants) upgrade the difficulty of {@skill Stealth} checks made against anyone using the primal radar once. In areas of medium vegetation (such as a garden), upgrade the difficulty of {@skill Stealth} checks made against anyone using the primal radar twice. In areas of high vegetation (such as a thick jungle), {@skill Stealth} checks made against someone using the primal radar are "Impossible" checks. Even if the user of the primal radar cannot see or hear a character trying to remain unnoticed while in medium range of the user, they must still make a {@skill Stealth} check.
{@i You may only use the primal radar if you have ranks in the {@skill Primal} skill.}
{@b Author:} Craftidore

gear.name: Portable Barrier Dome
description: Developed by combining magic and technology, Portable Barrier Domes are created by casting a variation of a {@spell Barrier} spell on a small containment device. The containment device is then imbued with a stabilizing spell to create a lasting effect. The user may take a maneuver to pull out and/or activate the PBD. This will create a dome shaped force field around themselves (engaged range) and protect them from ranged attacks.

All ranged attacks against the character with the device deal damage to the dome instead. The dome has a Wound Threshold of 9, which fully regenerates after 1 day. If the dome exceeds its threshold, it is destroyed and the device overheats, destroying it one step.

The PBD cannot prevent pure magic (such as {@spell Attack|attack spells}) and can be affected by anti magic spells and devices (such as {@spell Dispel}), as well as being instantly deactivated (and destroyed 1 step) by EMP blasts.
{@b Author:} Silvak the Judge

gear.name: Blunder Knucks
description: This device is a finger-less half glove with a rigid strip of conductive material across the knuckles and an embedded micro-battery in the palm. A close-quarters weapon, blunder knucks are designed to disable foes and their armor.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Boarding Mace
description: In tight compartments, surrounded by vital machinery and piping, {@gear Coil Gun|coil guns} and flare lenses quickly lead to catastrophic damage to ship systems. A well-balanced boarding mace, with its conductive head and hefty batteries, is the preferred weapon of many a deckhand.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Burner
description: This hand weapon emits a stream of agitated particles that quickly ignites light materials as easily as it does skin and flesh.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Molecular Thread
description: Consisting only of a thin, molded grip that can extend a molecule-thin line of thread at the press of a button, this weapon is a common self-defense device.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Coil Gun
description: A heavy weapon consisting of a thick battery pack and a long barrel encircled by a spiraling magnetic accelerator, a coil gun packs a big punch.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Flare Pistol
description: A flare pistol is a lensed weapon that emits a concentrated laser beam, ripping apart molecules in a thin line of destruction.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Flare Rifle
description: A larger, more powerful version of a {@gear flare pistol} that requires two hands to operate.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Stinger
description: A compact and easily concealed hand weapon that fires jacketed darts, this is a popular option for self-protection.
Add {@dice setback|2} to skill checks made to find this item when concealed.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Stun Ray
description: This wide-nosed hand weapon emits a pulse of disruptive energy, playing havoc with the electromagnetic systems of a living being. Stun rays only cause strain damage.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Armored Tunic
description: A fitted tunic with plates of impact resistant and energy dispersing material woven into the fabric.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Combat Armor
description: Consisting of thick plates of hardened material layered over an under-suit of protective mesh, this armor also has a self-contained pressure suit with two hours of breathable air when sealed. Sealing the combat armor requires a maneuver.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Deckhand's Belt
description: A common apparatus, this thick belt has a compact battery and bands of fibers that project a protective, energetic cushion when the wearer is struck.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Repulsion Field Generator
description: This heavy, fist-sized device produces a field of deflective energy around its user.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Adrenaline Hypo
description: This small, single use syringe works exactly like a {@gear Painkiller} (Page 95 of the {@title Genesys Core Rulebook}) but restoring Strain rather than Wounds.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Field Meter
description: This palm-sized device can detect radiation levels, electromagnetic currents, and even gravimetric variation.
Add {@dice boost} to {@skill Perception} and {@skill Vigilance} checks made while using a field meter. In addition, the GM may determine that there are narrative benefits to using this device.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Hand Radio
description: A common communication device with a range of up to orbital scale, though requiring line of sight (while ignoring minor obstructions like buildings or station walls).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Heel Rockets
description: When activated, these small rockets allow the user to fly or hover for the duration of one encounter, or ten minutes.
After use, the heel rockets' fuel cell must be recharged. This can be done at any shop that sells them, or at a fuel station, for 25 Sols.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Medical Case
description: Necessary to perform {@skill Medicine} checks to heal characters, the medical case also provides the benefit of either one {@gear palliative tonic} or {@gear adrenaline hypo} per encounter.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Palliative Tonic
description: This single use vial, when imbibed, works exactly like a {@gear Painkiller} (Page 95 of {@title Genesys Core Rulebook}).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Punch Card Machine
description: This device is required to perform {@skill Computers} checks to interact with computer terminals.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Slide Rule
description: A trusty slide rule greatly assists in any calculation.
Add {@dice boost} to any {@skill Computers} or {@skill Astrocartography} checks made while using a slide rule.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Standard Tool Kit
description: Required to perform {@skill Mechanics} checks to repair mechanical devices or {@archetype Robot} characters.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Lab Coat
description: In addition to lending an air of authority, lab coats also possess useful pockets and pouches of all sizes.
Add {@dice boost} to any {@skill Leadership} or {@skill Negotiation} checks made while wearing a lab coat and increase the {@rule encumbrance threshold} of the wearer by 2.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Ship's Suit
description: The common attire of ship hands everywhere, ship's suits are usually marked with the colors and crests of the ship that employs the wearer.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Ship's Suit (Tailored)
description: Officers tend to wear better made and more expensive versions of the common {@gear ship's suit}.
Add {@dice boost} to all social checks made while wearing a tailored ship's suit.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

gear.name: Space Suit
description: Space suits are needed for extra-vehicular activities and when exploring environments that lack a breathable atmosphere. Modern space suits are sleek and form fitting, while older models are quite bulky and stiff. For an older space suit, reduce the cost to 300 Sols and add {@dice setback} to all {@skill Athletics} and {@skill Coordination} checks made while wearing the suit.
Once sealed, which takes a maneuver, the suit provides 3 hours of breathable air.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

rule.name: Magitek Crafting Rules
description: A weapon may be granted the {@quality Primal Magitek}, {@quality Divine Magitek}, or {@quality Arcane Magitek} item qualities provided the weapon does not already possess a Magitek item quality. In order to do this, a character must succeed at a {@difficulty hard|Artifice}. If successful, decrease the weapon's base damage by one and give it one Magitek item quality. The upgrade process requires 150 credits/dollars/generic currency worth of materials and 3 hours of work. The average price to have someone else upgrade it is 300 credits/dollars/generic currency.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

quality.name: Primal Magitek
description: When making a combat check with this weapon, add {@symbols a} per rank in {@skill Primal}.
If the user has no ranks in {@skill Primal}, add {@dice setback|2} to the check.

The Primal Magitek weapon quality should only apply to weapons which allow the user to increase their effectiveness by channeling their magic into them. Weapons which use magical technology but are operated the same regardless of magical affinity should not possess this weapon quality.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

quality.name: Divine Magitek
description: When making a combat check with this weapon, add {@dice boost} per rank in {@skill Divine}.
If the user has no ranks in {@skill Divine}, add {@dice setback|2} to the check.

The Divine Magitek weapon quality should only apply to weapons which allow the user to increase their effectiveness by channeling their magic into them. Weapons which use magical technology but are operated the same regardless of magical affinity should not possess this weapon quality.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

quality.name: Arcane Magitek
description: When a successful combat check with this weapon is made, the user treats the base damage as the normal base damage plus their ranks in {@skill Arcana}.
If the user has no ranks in {@skill Arcana}, add {@dice setback|2} to the check.

The Arcane Magitek weapon quality should only apply to weapons which allow the user to increase their effectiveness by channeling their magic into them. Weapons which use magical technology but are operated the same regardless of magical affinity should not possess this weapon quality.
{@b Author:} Craftidore

skill.name: Artifice
description: The Artifice skill allows your character to build, disassemble, repair, or modify anything which works via magical technology (regardless of whether or not such items have a Magitek item quality). It can be used to fix the engines on a magical airship or increase the range of the telepathically linked radios.

If your Space Fantasy game has no prevalent mundane technology, only magical technology, use this skill in place of {@skill Mechanics}. If both magical technology and mundane technology are prevalent then use both Artifice and {@skill Mechanics}, but (with your GM's permission) when you select a career for your character with the {@skill Mechanics} skill, you may choose to make the Artifice skill a career skill instead.
{@b Author:} Craftidore
shouldUse: Your character needs to repair a damaged weapon, vehicle, or other piece of equipment which uses magical technology.
Your character wants to sabotage something which uses magical technology.
Your character wishes to add the {@quality Primal Magitek}, {@quality Divine Magitek}, or {@quality Arcane Magitek} item qualities to a weapon (see {@rule Magitek Crafting Rules}).
shouldNotUse: You are trying to repair or work with mundane technology (use {@skill Mechanics}).
You are trying to cast a spell or power something of magical technology with magic (use {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Divine}, or {@skill Primal}).

You are trying to operate magical technology which doesn't require knowledge of its inner workings to use (like how people use phones without knowing how they work on the inside) (use {@skill Operating}).

career.name: Doc
description: Sooner or later, everyone needs to see the Doc.

A Doc has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Charm}, {@skill Cool}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Leadership}, {@skill Medicine}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Knowledge}, {@skill Resilience}. A Doc chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Doc characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:
gear: {@gear Ship's Suit (Tailored)|Tailored Ship's Suit} or {@gear Lab Coat}

career.name: Egghead
description: From the calculation chamber to the fusion control deck, every good ship needs an Egghead.

An Egghead has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Astrocartography}, {@skill Computers}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Gunnery}, {@skill Knowledge}, {@skill Negotiation}, {@skill Operating}, {@skill Perception}. An Egghead chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Egghead characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:
gear: {@gear Ship's Suit (Tailored)|Tailored Ship's Suit} or {@gear Lab Coat}

career.name: Grease Monkey
description: When it is really broken, call a Grease Monkey to fix it.

A Grease Monkey has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Brawl}, {@skill Coordination}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Mechanics}, {@skill Negotiation}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Piloting}, {@skill Vigilance}. A Grease Monkey chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Grease Monkey characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:
gear: 2 {@gear Palliative Tonic|Palliative Tonics} and 1 {@gear Adrenaline Hypo}

career.name: Jack of All Trades
description: Often a second or third mate, a Jack of All Trades is essential crew.

A Jack of All Trades has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Mechanics}, {@skill Medicine}, {@skill Melee}, {@skill Negotiation}, {@skill Piloting}, {@skill Ranged (Light)}, {@skill Skulduggery}, {@skill Streetwise}. A Jack of All Trades chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Jack of All Trades characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:

career.name: Muscle
description: When push comes to shove, the Muscle does the shoving.

The Muscle has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Brawl}, {@skill Cool}, {@skill Coercion}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Melee}, {@skill Ranged (Heavy)}, {@skill Streetwise}, {@skill Vigilance}. The Muscle chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Muscle characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:
gear: {@gear Coil Gun} or {@gear Blunder Knucks} and {@gear Boarding Mace}
2 {@gear Palliative Tonic|Palliative Tonics} and 1 {@gear Adrenaline Hypo}

career.name: Rocket Jockey
description: Only a certain type of person has the mixture of talent and raw confidence necessary to be a Rocket Jockey.

A Rocket Jockey has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Astrocartography}, {@skill Charm}, {@skill Coordination}, {@skill Cool}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Gunnery}, {@skill Operating}, {@skill Piloting}. A Rocket Jockey chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Rocket Jockey characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:

career.name: Skipper
description: The Skipper is where the buck stops, and a good one earns their crew's unquestionable loyalty.

A Skipper has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Coercion}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Gunnery}, {@skill Leadership}, {@skill Operating}, {@skill Perception}, {@skill Ranged (Light)}, {@skill Resilience}. A Skipper chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Skipper characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:
gear: 2 {@gear Palliative Tonic|Palliative Tonics} and 1 {@gear Adrenaline Hypo}

career.name: Smooth Talker
description: A ship's purser or ship's agent is almost always a Smooth Talker, using their innate charm to forward the crew's interest.

A Smooth Talker has the following skills as career skills: {@skill Charm}, {@skill Cool}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Discipline}, {@skill Negotiation}, {@skill Streetwise}, {@skill Vigilance}. A Smooth Talker chooses four of these career skills and gains one rank in each before spending experience (XP).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt
Rather than spending currency during character creation, players with Smooth Talker characters may instead choose to start with the following gear:
gear: 2 {@gear Palliative Tonic|Palliative Tonics} and 1 {@gear Adrenaline Hypo}

archetype.name: Irongall

description: Irongalls begin with one rank in {@skill Resilience}. You still cannot train their {@skill Resilience} above rank 2 during character creation.

During their training and cultivation, the Irongalls endure decades of painful growth of generations of ironwasp larvae. The galls the larvae leave behind fortify the Irongalls with a sturdy bark that fears neither axe nor fire nor laser pistol. Irongalls patrol the lands of the Consortium and protect their slender brethren.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetype.name: Pettler

description: Pettlers begin with one rank in {@skill Negotiation}. You still cannot train their {@skill Negotiation} above rank 2 during character creation.

With careful pruning, a Pettler's incredible floral arrangements will attract outsiders to their even more incredible deals. A relatable face always seems to set the outsiders at ease, and the mind-altering pheromones are just an added bonus. Pettlers can typically be found on trade and diplomacy missions to secure wealth and fertile soil for the Consortium.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetype.name: Carniflor

description: Carniflors begin with one rank in {@skill Stealth}. You still cannot train their {@skill Stealth} above rank 2 during character creation.

Divergent evolution has turned the Carniflors away from blessed sunlight, towards a more expeditious (and bloody) source of nutrition. They sometimes have difficulty distinguishing between friend-meat and meat-meat. Carniflors are typically sent on missions to stalk and hunt the enemies of the Consortium in whatever dark corners they hide.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetype.name: Fibian

description: Fibians begin with one (1) rank in {@skill Mechanics}. They still cannot train {@skill Mechanics} above rank 2 during character creation.

Fibians come from a swampy world on the outer edge of civilized space. Like many humanoids, their history is marred by warfare, but as they became a space-faring people, their planet was united. They are an industrious species and almost all Fibians take an active interest in learning how things work from a very early age.

{@b Appearance:} Fibians are strong, frog-like humanoids standing roughly the same height as most humans. They have bald, frog-like heads and very wrinkly necks. Their hands and feet are webbed, and most Fibians spend more time out of water than in it.

{@b Society:} Throughout most of their history, Fibians were tribal. After the great unification of the tribes, their society started to more closely resemble that of other interstellar worlds. Still, honor is a very important quality to the Fibians, and they are known for their loyalty and honesty. They are often mechanics, pilots, or other careers involving machinery, as such workings are often revered as almost divine in nature.
{@b Author:} Chris Markham

archetypeAbility.name: Alloyed Galls
description: Your character's soak is increased by one.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetypeAbility.name: Photosynthesis
description: Spending six (6) hours in abundant light with adequate water allows you to produce enough nutrients to survive for a week.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetypeAbility.name: Lumbering
description: When you suffer strain to perform a second maneuver, spend one (1) additional strain.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetypeAbility.name: Ambrosial Aroma
description: Add {@symbols a} to {@skill Charm}, {@skill Negotiation}, and {@skill Leadership} checks targeting creatures within Short range who can smell.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetypeAbility.name: Barbed Vines
description: Your character adds the quality {@quality Ensnare|Ensnare 1} to their {@skill Melee} and {@skill Brawl} combat checks.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetypeAbility.name: Digestive Enzymes
description: Once per encounter, a Carniflor character may use an action to dissolve and absorb the nutrients from an {@rule incapacitated} organic creature. If they do, they may heal any combination of wounds or strain totalling the value of the consumed creature's silhouette.
{@b Author:} Flame112

archetypeAbility.name: Amphibious
description: Fibians are able to breathe water as well as air, and do not treat water as {@rule Difficult and Impassable Terrain|difficult terrain}.
{@b Author:} Chris Markham

archetypeAbility.name: Leap
description: Fibians may spend a maneuver to horizontally jump from up to Medium range to engage an opponent; if making a vertical jump, a Fibian may leap up to anywhere within Short range.
{@b Author:} Chris Markham

archetypeAbility.name: Swamp Dweller
description: Fibians add {@dice boost} to {@skill Stealth} checks made in a swamp environment.
{@b Author:} Chris Markham

adversary.name: Artificer
gear: {@gear Artificer's Gear}: add {@symbols s} to checks this character makes to repair or fix magical technology
description: Artificers work on magical technology. This career requires them to be good at a lot of things. They need to know how to artifice, have a bit of working knowledge about all types of magic, and decent ability to operate the devices they create.

adversary.name: Morgessa
description: This proud and athletic woman is one of the Despot of Vordun's most trusted agents, and commands perfect loyalty from those in her charge.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Vordun Thug
description: Conditioned to serve unquestioningly and enhanced with experimental stimulants, these dangerous men and women are the Despot's most effective enforcers.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Yortin Fleinn

abilities.name: Natural
abilities.description: Once per session, may reroll one {@skill Stealth} or {@skill Skulduggery} check ({@title Genesys} Core Rulebook, p.79).

description: A man well-known around Gymir's seedy underbelly as a sneak thief and burglar. Available to steal anything for the right price.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Nine Sisters Security
description: Well dressed and well built, these local professionals are just trying to keep things peaceful.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Sharan Joels
description: An experienced agent for Solarian Intelligence that has spent a bit too long undercover.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Anju
description: Inquisitive, funny, and smart, this Daradeen noble is hard not to like.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Old Mining Robot
description: This massive industrial robot has been reprogrammed as a trap for the unwary.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Gertra
description: A silver haired, stern but charismatic cult leader with a big vision for her followers and the future of her order.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversary.name: Follower of Disa
description: Immersed in tales of the old ways, these cultists cannot be reasoned with.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversaryAbility.name: Live to Fight Again
description: Once per session, may use this ability as an incidental to have this adversary escape the current encounter. However this happens, the adversary may not return to the encounter. The GM might decide that this ability cannot be used in some locations/situations.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversaryAbility.name: Metamorphic Serum
description: Once per encounter, this character may use this ability as a maneuver to inject themselves with a metamorphic reagent which causes their muscles to bulge and their fingers sprout long claws. They increase their {@characteristic Brawn} and Soak by 2 and gain the following attack profile: Claws ({@skill Melee}; Damage +3; Crit 3).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversaryAbility.name: Born Leader
description: Once per round, may suffer 3 Strain to perform the Born Leader maneuver to upgrade an allied character's next skill check.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

adversaryAbility.name: Stomp
description: Once per turn this adversary can perform the Stomp action to shake the environment with its heavy footfalls, triggering an out-of-turn {@difficulty hard|Coordination} for enemies within medium range. Failure knocks the enemy {@rule prone}, while each {@symbols h} generated causes one wound.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

vehicle.name: Saucer-class Shuttle
description: Nearly ubiquitous in settled space, this six-seater craft is a capable shuttle used for landing on the surface of moons and small planets. These craft can also be outfitted with heavier weapons, sacrificing passenger and cargo capacity to instead play the role of a star fighter.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

vehicle.name: Attack Saucer
description: When outfitted as a fighter craft, the {@vehicle Saucer-class Shuttle|Saucer's} {@rule Handling} is reduced to 0, Passenger Capacity to 0, Encumbrance Capacity to 6, and the following weapon profiles replace the existing profile: Paired Light Flare Lenses (Fire Arc Forward; Damage 2; Critical 3; Range [Short]; {@quality Linked|Linked 1}).
Torpedo Launcher (Fire Arc Forward; Damage 6; Critical 3; Range [Long]; {@quality Blast|Blast 4}, {@quality Breach|Breach 2}, {@quality Limited Ammo|Limited Ammo 2}).
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

vehicle.name: Baadal-class Shuttle
description: This sleek, arrowhead-shaped craft is the standard Daradeen shuttle. Nimble, and sporting a powerful accelerator cannon, this craft is suited to transport high-value passengers.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

vehicle.name: Kissimmee-class Cutter

weapons.name: 1 Port and 1 Starboard Forward-Mounted Paired Flare Lenses
Battery of 5 Port Mounted Heavy Accelerator Cannons
Battery of 5 Starboard Mounted Heavy Accelerator Cannons

description: A well-built and durable ship, the Kissimmee-class Cutter is favored by merchant escort and light transport crews for its versatility and dependability. Able to accept a wide variety of parts and relatively easy to retrofit, this class has been in service for several decades.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

vehicle.name: Ca Den Raider-class Frigate

weapons.name: 1 Port and 1 Starboard Forward-Mounted Paired Flare Lenses
1 Port and 1 Starboard Rear-Mounted Paired Flare Lenses
2 Batteries of 5 Port Mounted Heavy Accelerator Cannons
2 Batteries of 5 Starboard Mounted Heavy Accelerator Cannons

abilities.name: Shuttle Complement
abilities.description: 2 {@vehicle Saucer-class Shuttle|Saucer-class Shuttles}, 4 {@vehicle Attack Saucer|Attack Saucers}

description: This sturdy and well-armed warship serves as the backbone of the Vordunish fleet. Two Ca Dens are enough to subdue a small colony or space station, and a single Raider can often withstand a Solarian Cruiser's barrage long enough to ignite their out-sized fusion drive and escape the larger vessel.
{@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

vehicle.name: Chaandanee-class Sloop

weapons.name: 1 Port and 1 Starboard Forward-Mounted Paired Flare Lenses

description: Daradeen ships are advanced, and punch well above their weight. The experimental Chaandanee-class Sloop is no exception, being as fast as other vessels of its class but better armored and carrying heavier weapons. This small, versatile warship will fill many roles for the Daradeen navy, from light patrol to convoy escort to transport of vital personnel.

setting.name: Mechanism, "Chanis," The Clockwork System
summary: Chanis is a massive artificial gigastructure orbiting a small red dwarf star colloquially known as Lus. Whatever naturally occurring planets may have once populated the Chanis system, they have long since been harvested and rendered down to provide the raw materials for the current Chanis gigastructure.

Chanis comprises a number of components. Gris, a ringworld orbital ring, circumscribes Lus. A secondary and also inhabited ring, Igris, is made of enormous semi-rigidly tethered rectangular tiles and provides a diurnal cycle to Gris. Lusleen is a hollowed out moon-turned-megapolis and anchors Igris. Lusleen is the primary port of harbor and trade hub of Chanis. Finally, there is the Riverbelt, a stream of pulverized and constantly colliding spacial objects caught in the shielding mechanism that loosely wraps around all sides of Gris, provides a constantly shifting starscape to the night skies as well as a buffer against dangers such as comets and asteroids entering into Chanis and threatening Gris. The Riverbelt is also a major hazard, making it difficult to actually land ships anywhere on Gris, thus providing the ringworld and its myriad species and cultures a rather severe incidental isolation.

Chanis can be lifted to any science fiction or science fantasy setting. As conceived, though, it is firmly in the science fantasy genre and acts as a point of confluence for many magic influences, be they leylines, colliding dimensions, a universal mystic little-"f" force that may be in certain unnamed properties well known to players of the {@title Genesys} system, or otherwise. Using the special properties of Chanis' multiple gigantic components, these magical influences are harvested and redistributed throughout the system to power, among other things, the Riverbelt, the countless slight adjustments necessary to maintain the sublimely synchronized orbits of Gris and Igris, life support systems in Igris and Lusleen, and modulations of Lus' stellar atmosphere that would otherwise make such a (relatively speaking) tight orbit of a red dwarf star totally inhospitable to any life or even stable formulations. Moreover, the Riverbelt and the underside of Gris, which is engraved with enormous planet-sized runes, interact in such a way that the materials of the Riverbelt deposit into Gris' underside and perpetually heal the structure and maintain the structural integrity of the ringworld.

items: A clue from an adventure in another system has brought the PCs to Chanis. The clue brings them first to Lusleen, where they find out that it is actually related to an isolated civilization on the surface of Gris. The civilization is hostile to outsiders and the PCs must successfully navigate the Riverbelt to reach the civilization.

Chanis is a great weapon of cosmic proportions! A villain has discovered that Chanis can be wielded in such a way that the planet-ending forces of the red dwarf, Lus, are directed through the interstitial void in between points in space to impact and obliterate planets anywhere in the galaxy. The PCs must stop the villain from gaining control of this incredible weapon--or perhaps they are the ones intent on uncovering its use and invoking its enormous power.

lore.title: Lus
entries: A small red dwarf star, Lus is modulated by the orbital system that surrounds it. However, solar patterns are still somewhat unpredictable, with sunspot swarms and mild flares relatively frequent. As a result, Gris and Igris tend to have likewise somewhat unpredictable, albeit fairly mild, seasons and seasonal weather. Due to Lus' influence, the difficulty of space navigation checks is upgraded once while made in Chanis or otherwise under the influence of Lus.

items: A spacecraft has entered dangerously close to Lus' corona and has become unresponsive. Mysterious and seemingly malicious incorporeal entities have overtaken the ship and they cannot be communicated with--they seem able to possess organics and ship systems with equal ease. The ship's technology is fairly advanced to allow it to get so close to a star and would make valuable salvage to a group that could retrieve it.

lore.title: Gris
entries: Gris is the primary inhabited "planet" of Chanis, and all of the habitable areas exist on the inner surface of the ring (i.e., the side facing Lus and Igris). Centrifugal force provides the majority of subjective gravity on the internal side of the ring and the inside edge is approximately 0.25 AU, or 235 million kilometers, from Lus. With a circumference of approximately 1476.5M km and an 11000km width, Gris has a habitable surface area of about 1.6242034e+13 square kilometers--or a crapton of real estate as it's known to most explorers (in comparison, Earth's surface area is 5.101e+9 square kilometers).

The diurnal period, due to the slightly slower rotational speed of Igris and its enormous rectangular shading tiles, of all inhabited regions of Gris is 26 hours split into 13 hour days and 13 hour nights. Grisians rarely track time beyond the diurnal period, as there is no significant seasonal variance. However, Gris completes a full rotation around Lus (a.k.a., a "year") approximately every 53.5 hours, given its tangential rotational speeds of around 1,220 km/s.

Gris' atmosphere is kept in the ring via an edgewall which extends 2000 km from the external (or "backside") of the ring. Enormous mountains characterize the edgewall, with plentiful sheer faces and often shifting or avalanching surfaces. The internal floor of Gris extends, on average, about 400 km above the backside. As a result, there are various "underdarks" made up of subterranean systems and expanses inhabited by unique flora and fauna throughout Gris.

Large, antenna-like towers that protrude from the rim of the edgewall at regular intervals are common attractions to spacefaring visitors to Chanis. These towers extend to (astronomically speaking) a fairly close range of counterpart antennae located on Lusleen. As the structures orbit within range of each other, magical energy transfers between them. This maintains a certain equilibrium within the greater structure of the entire Chanis system and is part of a cosmically sized circuit that soothes Lus (which would otherwise have wildly variable solar weather) and redirects and slows foreign objects such as meteors, comets, etc. approaching the system at dangerous vectors as a sort of shield.

Gris is inhabited by myriad different species and cultures across its massive habitable surface. These species and cultures are of varying characteristics and development, but generally are not actually spacefaring. Familiarity with magic and capacity for its use also varies greatly across groups. It is not uncommon for civilizations to be totally ignorant of most others on Gris and beyond. However, travel and adventure is common across the ringworld, and though only a small handful of starfaring cultures inhabit Gris, almost all are accustomed to totally alien visitors, technologies, and magics making their way through their regions.
Gris is a nexus of magical energies and all magic (or equivalent) related checks receive a {@dice boost} while on Gris.

items: A crash landing due to collisions in the Riverbelt has left the PCs stranded in a technologically primitive region of Gris. The PCs will need to supplement their ship repairs with magical artifacts from the area cultures to bring the ship up to capability to make it to Lusleen.

The PCs make first contact with a Grisian culture that resides, at least partially, in one of the many underdarks of the ring. The culture has no real knowledge beyond the immediately adjacent regions, and certainly is unfamiliar with spacefaring civilizations or the technology for such.

A city on Gris is under threat from meteor rains emanating from the Riverbelt! What started as a few, if highly unusual, meteor strikes in the outlying areas has rapidly become a meteor swarm of smaller objects. It seems things will get worse--more destructive and deadlier--before they get better. Without help from the PCs, the entire city is at risk of being pulverized out of existence.

A businessman from Lusleen wants the PCs to investigate a competitor's production facilities on Gris' surface. For an additional fee, the businessman would like the PCs to commit some light espionage and sabotage--or some heavy sabotage involving assassination for a proportionally larger fee.

lore.title: Igris
entries: Igris is a spiraling ribbon orbiting Lus just inside the orbit of Gris. Igris comprises an 11,000 km wide ribbon with eight (8) twists and orbit at a slightly slower rate than Gris, having an orbital period of 107 hours. As a result of the slower orbital period and twists, Gris experiences a diurnal cycle. As between Gris and Igris, the ribbon completes a rotational period every 53.5 hours.

Igris is home primarily to two different species that can exist in its harsh, sunwashed and airless environment: the Ethereals and the Automata. However, a number of domed cities and spaceports dot Igris' otherwise perfectly smooth and empty surface, on both the Lus-side and the Gris-side of Igris. The domed cities house various organic and other species that cannot survive that near-vacuum of Igris' surface.

The Ethereals are made of a smokey energy that somehow maintains a generally humanoid shape. The Ethereal civilization is unfathomably ancient and thought to be as old as Chanis (or at least its current construction) itself. According to legend and rumor, the Ethereals were originally constructs of whatever forces first built Chanis, intended to maintain Gris and Igris.

The Automata are not so much a species as much as a loosely related collection of sentient machine beings. The Automata are all that remains of a short-lived highly technological empire that conquered a substantial portion of Gris. Eventually the empire fell and the Automata fled to Igris where, due to the nature of their construction, they were able to flourish without worry of organic beings interfering (or enacting retribution for acts related to their imperial origin).

Another remarkable feature of Igris is that it is not a "complete" ring. Igris actually extends from polar opposite sides of Lusleen, securely anchored to the labyrinthine once-moon. As Lusleen is tidally locked to Lus, it helps secure and stabilize Igris' orbit.
Igris is a realm of shadows and contrasts. {@skill Stealth} checks on Igris receive a {@dice boost} and {@skill perception} checks receive a {@dice setback}.

items: A war is brewing between the Ethereals and the Automata. The PCs have been caught up in the middle of the conflict.
A mad Automata is attempting to destroy one of the dome cities of Igris! The PCs must find a way to stop them before their plans come to fruition and countless organics die or lose their homes!

Grob Nekrteks, a technonecromancer of little renown, has converted a dome city into Grobbers--strange hiveminded hybrids blending organic tissue and Automata technology and slaved to Grob's will. Grob and his Grobbers are expanding rapidly across Igris and rumor has it that Grob intends to sabotage Igris so that it collapses into Gris, giving the technonecromancer an endless supply of organic flesh and technological hardware to build his great technonecromantic empire!

lore.title: Lusleen
entries: Lusleen is, other than the red dwarf star Lus, perhaps the one remaining natural planetary structure in Chanis. Even then, however, Lusleen has been hollowed out over the eons to the point that the moon's surface is little more than a regolith skin wrapping a honeycombed interior of tunnels and chambers making up Lusleen's megalopolis. While about the size of Earth's moon, it is in fact half the total mass as a result of the endlessly mazing tunnels, caverns, catacombs, tramways, and the like.

Lusleen's surface has no atmosphere and, outside of the various spaceports scattered across the surface that lead directly into the internal city, is entirely devoid of both organic or constructed life. Two massive structures tangentially extend 3,000 km out of each of Lusleen's poles. These structures are used to harvest and distribute magical energies from Gris' rotation through the system-wide circuit of Chanis.

Lusleen's interior is home to an enormous chaotic metropolis. Various governments run various districts, but the general state of Lusleen is fairly anarchic. Crime syndicates run rampant and oligarchical business consortia are the ultimate wielders of power in Lusleen. More so than anywhere else in Chanis, Lusleen principally runs on money and power--and money is necessary to buy power.

The difficulty of finding items for sale on Lusleen is reduced once, to a minimum of {@difficulty easy}; however, all such checks are upgraded once. On a {@symbols d}, the PCs have run afoul of an oligarch and/or a local criminal syndicate, as appropriate.

items: An oligarch is recruiting offworlders to gather intelligence on the competition. Whatever the PCs ultimately uncover, the oligarch will demand they follow up with a little "aggressive espionage" or will put a bounty on their heads.
Criminal syndicates are going to war and the PCs better choose a side! There will be no neutral ground in this conflict.

Deep in Lusleen there is an abandoned section of the city that is rumored to house ancient laboratories still holding untold treasures. However, just because the area is abandoned, does not mean it is {@i uninhabited}.

lore.title: Riverbelt
entries: The Riverbelt is a vaguely defined region of pulverized materials caught in the various fields of force and influence that act as a mild sort of shield for Gris. Objects caught in the Riverbelt are pulverized to a fine dust in the Lus-facing side of the stream before being cycled to the side of the stream covering Gris' backside. The dust on the backside is absorbed into Gris itself to repair and maintain the various structures and systems keeping the ringworld sound.

The pulverizing side of the Riverbelt is a chaotic and dangerous place, where objects constantly collide and disintegrate each other into ever smaller pieces. Only the truly desperate hide in the Riverstream and call it home--but those who are able to survive the location are generally left in isolation. Occasionally pirates and other scoundrels will try to make a living in the Riverstream as ships necessarily have to pass through it if they wish to transit between the surface of Gris and Igris, Lusleen, or the greater cosmos beyond.

An aesthetically pleasant side-effect of the Riverstream is that it provides an artificial starry night sky to inhabitants of Gris, who would otherwise have nothing more than the pitch black of Igris above them for their night sky. Rather, the pulverizing objects reflect light back to Gris and give the Riverstream the appearance of an ever shifting and flowing starfield.

{@skill Piloting} checks in the Riverbelt are upgraded once. On a {@symbols d}, the PCs crashland on a roving asteroid and will need to make repairs quick before it inevitably collides with other objects in the Riverbelt!

items: Bounty hunters, Hawk and Hound, are on the prowl in the Riverbelt and are either hunting the PCs or have mistaken them for a different bounty. Hawk is an Automata able to fly independently through the void of the Riverbelt, and Hound is a sentient ship (organic, technological, or both) that primarily communicates through Hawk.

The PCs have been hired to shut down a pirate operation based out of the Riverbelt. The pirates have developed a way to protect larger asteroids from colliding with other objects in the Riverbelt and have inhabited a larger asteroid-turned-fortress.

A great race through the Riverbelt is starting soon! The race is deadly and few survive to the finish line, but the rewards are great–and the destroyed ships of those who fail to finish certainly make good bonus salvage.

setting.name: The Solar Republic!
summary: Taking inspiration from the space operas and planetary romances of the early-to-mid 20th century, {@b The Solar Republic!} mini-setting features anachronistic technology, themes of adventure and heroism, and an idealized vision of human endeavor common to the genre.

Smart-mouthed grease monkeys, dashing rocket jockeys, and an occasional jack-of-all-trades loyally accompany their skipper on daring adventures across the settled star systems of mankind. Punch card computers and reams of ticker tape, beeping field scanners and trusty slide rules, coil guns and stun rays are all part and parcel with fusion-rockets and saucer landing craft.
The remaining sections of this gazette give a brief but wide-ranging look at this mini-setting.

entries.title: Settled Space
entries: The first wave of human settlement left Sol on huge, slow-moving colony ships. These generation ships, packed with equipment of all kinds and crewed by humanity's finest, fanned out into nearby space. Centuries passed between the stars, and by the time the great seed-ships reached their destinations they were met by settlers who had out-paced them on smaller, faster, fusion driven rocket ships – a technology invented a century after the generation ships departed Sol.

Still, communication was slow and travel slower. Humanity developed in pockets, separated by vast and largely empty space. Whole cultures rose and fell with little to no outside contact. Not until the discovery of gating technology, a bending of space itself only possible at certain balance points at the edges of star systems, did humanity begin an uneven and sometimes violent re-assimilation into a common civilization.
Now, decades later, much of humankind is united under a single banner: {@b The Solar Republic!}

entries.title: The Despot of Vordun
entries: The largest thorn in the side of the Solar Republic is also the most dangerous. Once Commodore Harlas Ashrod, now known as the Despot of Vordun, this former hero of the Solar Republic renounced their position in the Solarian Fleet to carve out a crude empire of captured settlements and outposts at the far edge of colonized space. Sitting atop their throne of melted Solarian crests, the Despot of Vordun plots and schemes, planning to one day destroy the Solar Republic and rule all of humankind.

entries.title: Regency of Daradeen
entries: The Daradeen are an insular culture spanning three systems, with only loose trading ties to the Solar Republic. It is suspected that some long-ago conflict led to their self-isolation. Indeed, they possess powerful warships that patrol the boundaries of their territory and turn aside ships that seek entrance to their region of space, and trade is limited to a single port at the edge of Daradeen space.

The Solarian Council would love nothing more than to bring the Daradeen star systems (and their advanced navy) into the Republic. For now, the Council is happy enough to maintain good trade relations.

entries.title: Aliens?
entries: Humans in {@b The Solar Republic!} setting have not yet encountered sentient aliens, and in fact what life has been found has been of the single-celled variety. In the centuries of human settlement, however, cultures have diverged dramatically. Further, experimentation and engineered adaptation has led to wild variations in hair and skin color, and sometimes even more extreme changes in physiology.

lore.title: Section 4: Spacecraft
entries: Spacecraft in {@b The Solar Republic!} setting maneuver on high impulse plasma thrusters when near planetary systems, space stations, and engaged in ship-to-ship combat. This form of propulsion is represented by the Max Speed rating and in all ways follows the normal rules for vehicle combat as described in the {@title Genesys Core Rulebook}.

When traveling to the edge of a star system to reach a Gate-Point that allows rapid travel between stars, star ships engage their fusion rockets. It takes two rounds to cycle up a fusion drive, and once activated in the third round, the craft cannot change direction until the fusion drive is deactivated. When a ship's fusion drive is active, its speed is doubled.

It becomes nearly impossible to target a ship that has engaged its fusion drive, upgrading any combat checks targeting the vessel three times. Further, it is extremely dangerous to pursue a ship with an active fusion drive too closely. When within Long range a {@rule Dangerous Driving} action is required instead of the {@rule Reposition} Maneuver to close one range band. {@symbols hh} generated on this check result in a vehicle critical hit for the pursuer as fusion exhaust sweeps across their ship.

It should be noted that it generally takes several weeks to a few months of travel under fusion drive to reach a Gate-Point. A successful {@skill Astrocartography} check is needed to plot a Gate-Jump, and then a successful {@skill Computers} check is required to create a punch card for the massive Gate Processing Computer. Once these steps have been completed and the ship has reached the jump point, the actual jump is instantaneous. Of course, another period of weeks or months is required to reach the inner system of the target star.

characterOptions.title: Section 2: New Starting Character Options
entries: In keeping with the genre exemplified by early-to-mid 20th century science fiction, the character options in this section are flavored with a touch of dashing bravado and anachronistic flare. In no way are these descriptions meant to limit players' characterizations, and have been written to exclude the darker bias of that bygone era.
{@b The Solar Republic!} setting is in all ways meant to be inclusive, drawing on the wonder and inspirational spirit of the possibilities of humanity.
After all, the future belongs to us all!

entries.title: Archetypes
entries: {@b The Solar Republic!} campaign setting uses the following archetypes from the {@title Genesys Core Rulebook}:

entries.title: {@archetype Average Human|The Average Human}, {@archetype The Laborer|Laborer}, {@archetype The Intellectual|Intellectual}, or {@archetype The Aristocrat|Aristocrat}
entries: These archetypes represent the basic variations in humanity found across the worlds and star systems settled by the human diaspora.

entries.title: {@archetype Mongrel|The Mongrel}
entries: This archetype represents a character who has been subject to experimentation by some exiled scientist or perhaps exposed to an alien microbe.

entries.title: {@archetype Animalistic Alien}
entries: This archetype represents engineered changes made by various settlements of humans to better adapt to the planets on which they live. No sentient aliens have (yet) been found by humans in {@b The Solar Republic!} setting, but there are dramatic biological variations in the human diaspora across settled space.

entries.title: {@archetype Robot}
entries: This archetype represents the sentient robots that have been built to replace or supplement human labor. Fully sentient robots are rare, but not unheard of. The Republic has yet to pass a set of universal laws to govern robots, so each port or settled planet must decide for themselves how robots are treated.
Robots in {@b The Solar Republic!} setting most often resemble the shiny humanoid-shaped constructions found in the fiction of the early- to mid-20th century.
Rather than the {@b {@archetypeAbility Networked Intelligence}} special ability, increase a Robot's starting experience to 185.

entries: {@b The Solar Republic!} setting has several careers for players to choose from for their characters, styled to capture the spirit of the genre.
If the GM allows, players may choose to take the starting equipment package for their chosen career, rather than spending currency during {@b Step 7} of character creation.
