entries: {@b Author:} Ryall Hyatt

In this short adventure, the PCs have a dangerous encounter with henchmen of the dastardly Despot of Vordun. The characters quickly discover an evil plot that may lead to the Despot's victory over the Solar Republic. Pursuing the Despot's minions will take the PCs to forgotten asteroid caves and aboard a beautiful prototype star ship. Will the heroes help to protect the Republic and thwart the Despot's plan? Will they seek fame and glory, or are they only interested in a reward of cold hard cash? And will they be tempted by the love of a mysterious royal somehow central to the Despot's plot?

entries.title: The Solar Republic!
entries: {@i An Adventure and Mini-Setting Gazette}

Gather your crew and board your fusion rocket ship for an adventure-packed visit to Epsilon Eridani. Intrigue, ray guns, and punch-card computers await in this {@setting Space Opera} adventure setting, {@b {@setting The Solar Republic!}}

entries.title: In This Gazette…
entries: In the first chapter of this booklet the reader will find a short adventure, suitable for three to five players, meant to be played in one to three sessions. Here also are descriptions of marvelous locations interspersed with the adventure's narrative. At the end of this chapter are included several adversary profiles mentioned in the adventure.

The second chapter of the booklet contains a brief synopsis of {@b {@setting The Solar Republic!}} adventure setting along with new careers, setting specific weapons and gear, and a few of the ships common to the setting.
Along with the {@title Genesys Core Rulebook} and a set of Genesys dice, this Gazette contains everything you need to run an adventure in {@b {@setting The Solar Republic!}} campaign setting.

chapters.title: Section 1: Gymir Station
entries: A popular stop on the Dalin trade run, Port Gymir is a hub-and-wheel style space station and small repair yard in orbit of the gas giant Aegir in the Epsilon Eridani system. Positioned inside Republic space, it is not uncommon to see Solarian Fleet patrol ships docked to the station's long central spires. While the saloons, clubs, and dancehalls of the station's commercial ring are known for their rowdy crowds, and many of Aegir's smaller moons play host to smugglers and semi-legal enterprises, Port Gymir is considered by most ships' captains a safe place to lay over and refuel.

The space station itself consists of one large and two smaller wheels spinning around a long central hub and docking spires. The three rings are connected by sturdy spokes to the central structure, with the two smaller rings rotating in opposition to the larger one. The large, outer ring is the habitation wheel, with housing and independent life support, as well as expansive hydroponics facilities. The two smaller, inner rings are dedicated to commercial enterprise and power generation, respectively. The spokes are structural, but also contain power conduits and elevators for travel to the central hub. The hub contains station security and control, and long spires extend outward from the station's center in either direction to provide docking facilities for visiting spacecraft.

entries.title: Why Gymir?
entries: The PCs may have stopped at Port Gymir to resupply or refuel their ship, or they may have needed repairs available at the port's shipyards. The PCs might be seeking a respite from adventure and want to enjoy the station's dancehalls, famous for their bawdy entertainment. The station is also a place to find work for a crew of traders, smugglers, or guns-for-hire.

entries.title: A Ship, a Ship!
entries: This adventure assumes that the PCs are senior officers aboard a trading and light escort starship (a {@vehicle Kissimmee-class Cutter} as detailed in the second section of this Gazetteer), and that said ship is already docked at Gymir Station. Have the players choose an appropriately adventurous name for their vessel - something like Ganymede's Veil, or The Flare Runner.

entries.title: As All Good Stories Do
entries: The adventure begins in a nightclub, the Nine Daughters Hall. A big band, twenty players strong, commands the main stage, belting out a neo-swing number that has the dance floor jumping. A full-throated singer lays soaring vocals across the hard-hitting rhythm and biting hooks. The air is smoky and alight with the glow of cigarillos, the haze pierced by two spotlights shining down from a catwalk far above.

The PCs are somewhere in the club, perhaps at the bar ordering a drink, perhaps on the floor with a newly met dance partner, or perhaps enjoying a proper meal for the first time in months at one of the white-clad tables that ring the dance floor.

{@skill Ranged (Heavy)} weapons are not allowed in the Nine Daughters Hall, and {@adversary Nine Sisters Security|security} will have their eye on any characters otherwise armed. Add {@dice setback} to {@skill Stealth} or {@skill Skulduggery} rolls that an obviously armed character makes.

entries.title: A Matter of Price
entries: A scuffle breaks out near one of the PCs, between an aggressive, broad-shouldered woman in a tailored ship's suit and a slim man in a shiny silver tunic. The woman has a hold on the man's tunic, and she uses her leverage to pull and shake him. She shoves him, sending the man on a collision course with one of the PCs.
A successful {@difficulty average|Coordination} will avoid the collision, allowing the man to fall {@rule prone} at the PC's feet. Failure results in the PC also being knocked {@rule prone}.

A successful {@difficulty hard|Athletics} will allow the PC to catch the man and avoid the collision. Other PCs may wish to scan the crowd or gather more information about the woman. Immediately, they see two other toughs clad in ship's suits with markings that match the woman's own. A successful {@difficulty average|Perception} reveals the following:

items: The woman is armed with a {@gear Burner} and is wearing a {@gear Deckhand's Belt}. Her companions are each armed with a {@gear Stinger}.
The club's {@adversary Nine Sisters Security|security personnel} have noticed the disturbance but are not moving to stop it.

entries: Read or paraphrase the following:
The man in the silver tunic, face turning red, protests, 'You agreed to half upfront, Morgessa, and I won't be intimidated into less.'
'How dare you argue with me, you petty thief! You'll take what I give you, and like it, Fleinn.'
The woman, Morgessa, is now flanked by her two henchmen.
'I have friends of my own,' says Fleinn. 'As you will soon learn.'
Morgessa's eyes turn to the PC.

Initiative can be rolled here, and a structured encounter can begin. {@adversary Morgessa} and her {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} intend to rough up {@adversary Yortin Fleinn} and any of his compatriots. They begin the encounter assuming that the PC is one of their targets.

A successful {@difficulty hard|Charm or Coercion} will convince Morgessa that the PC is unaffiliated with the man they intend to intimidate. Otherwise, and if the {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} act first, one of Morgessa's {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} attacks the PC and the other attacks Fleinn. Morgessa stands back, using her {@talent Inspiring Rhetoric (Improved)} talent to bolster her henchmen.

The {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} do not draw their weapons, using their fists instead. PCs who draw their weapons will be targeted by the club's {@adversary Nine Sisters Security|security people} who have been bribed by Morgessa to stay out of the fistfight. {@adversary Nine Sisters Security|Security} will tell them to holster their weapons and enforce the command with their {@gear Stun Ray|Stun Rays} and {@gear Boarding Mace|Boarding Maces}.
If Morgessa's original target is {@rule incapacitated}, she gloats for a moment and then exits the scene.

If Morgessa and her {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} become outnumbered, Morgessa drops below half of her wound or strain threshold, or one of her henchmen is {@rule incapacitated}, she immediately withdraws from the fight, using her {@b {@adversaryAbility Live to Fight Again}} ability.
If the PCs question Yortin Fleinn, a successful {@difficulty average|Charm or Coercion} or a small bribe can reveal any of the following:

items: Morgessa hired Fleinn to steal an item through an off-station contact.
Fleinn knows that Morgessa represents a powerful interest, but no specifics.
The item is in Ambassador Sudh's residence, envoy from Daradeen.
The item is a jewel called the Sapphire Lily. Fleinn does not know why Morgessa wants the item.

entries: A successful {@difficulty average|Knowledge} can reveal any of the following about the Daradeen:

items: The Regency of Daradeen is an insular culture that spans three systems and possesses advanced starships.
While contact is limited, they do trade with the Solar Republic and have an ambassador on Gymir Station.
Daradeen are gender fluid as a rule, and even have a fluid biological expression.

entries: If the PCs somehow capture one of Morgessa's thugs, he will bite down on a hollow tooth that contains a deadly toxin before answering questions.

Examining a thug's body, or if a PC managed to pick-pocket a thug earlier, discovers a ship's badge that bears the sigil of the Despot of Vordun and a small hardcase with 2 {@gear Adrenaline Hypo|adrenaline hypos} and a mystery syringe. A {@difficulty hard|Medicine} reveals the syringe contains {@adversaryAbility Metamorphic Serum|metamorphic serum} (see {@adversary Vordun Thug} profile later in this gazette). The same check, or a separate successful {@difficulty average|Medicine} of the body, finds numerous injection scars.
A successful {@difficulty easy|Knowledge} can impart the following about the Despot of Vordun:

items: A former hero of the Solarian Navy, the Despot now seeks to rule the Solar Republic.
The conflict is at a near stalemate despite the Solarian advantage in numbers, as the Despot is crafty and willing to sacrifice his troops.

entries: Fleinn does not hang around for long, saying he has other business to attend.

entries.title: Hard to Refuse
entries: The PCs may be interested enough to pursue the Despot's plot on their own. If not, or if at any point the GM wants to increase the stakes, they are approached by a woman who introduces herself as {@adversary Sharan Joels}, of Solarian Intelligence.
Agent Joels knows Morgessa is an agent of the Despot of Vordun. Solarian assets are spread thin, and so she is enlisting the PCs to disrupt Morgessa's plan, whatever it is.
Agent Joels appeals to the PCs' patriotism first, then offers a reward of 10k Sols, then informs the PCs that their ship will be impounded until and unless they stop Morgessa.

The agent could well become a thorn in the PCs' side, spurring them on when they get stuck by revealing information they missed. She can be aggressive and annoying, which will be all the better when she is revealed to be a double agent later.

entries.title: On the Trail
entries: If the PCs want to ask around the seedier side of the Station, a successful {@difficulty average|Streetwise} will reveal any of the following:

items: Morgessa has been trying to hire a sneakthief or picklock for a tough job.
Fleinn has spread the word that Morgessa cannot be trusted.

entries: For information about the Daradeen ambassador, an {@difficulty average|Charm or Coercion} at a nightlife establishment reveals any of the following:

items: Ambassador Sudh loves the nightlife of Gymir station and can often be found at the I Lopt Gambling Parlor.
The ambassador is hosting guests from Daradeen, who arrived on a {@vehicle Baadal-class Shuttle|Baadal-class shuttle} rather than docking their advanced starship with the station.

entries.title: Well Met
entries: If the PCs want to find the ambassador it is easy to track them down at the I Lopt Gambling Parlor. Accompanying Ambassador Sudh are two important Daradeen guests who are on a visit to the station. Representative Gnanik is older and officious, while the attaché {@adversary Anju} is young and curious. The three stand at a Centauri roulette table as bets are placed. A Daradeen security officer is close by, armed with a {@gear Flare Rifle}.
Upon being informed of the plot to steal an item from their residence, Ambassador Sudh realizes their passkey is missing. Gnanik and Anju immediately become alarmed.
Read or paraphrase the following:
Gnanik grabs at the ambassador's sleeve, angrily asking, 'Ambassador, do you realize what this could mean?'
'Stay calm, honored one. I must have dropped the passkey at the saloon. My security will protect…'
'We must return to your residence at once,' Gnanik interrupts.
'Ah but the game has barely begun…'
'The very future of Daradeen is at stake, Ambassador,' says the bright-eyed Anju. 'If the Lily falls into the wrong hands the consequences are unthinkable.'
Ambassador Sudh blushes in embarrassment and bows to the younger Daradeen.
'Of course, you are correct. Perhaps these dashing folks can be convinced to join us.' The Ambassador turns to the PCs. 'They seem to be informed on whatever is afoot.'

On the way to the Ambassador's residence, a successful {@difficulty average|Charm} will cause one of the Daradeen to reveal the existence of the Sapphire Lily. {@symbols t} generated on the check can reveal that the possessor of the Lily can demand the future regent of Daradeen's hand in marriage.

The Daradeen, if asked, say that the regent-to-be is aboard a nearby ship. A successful {@difficulty hard|Vigilance} reveals that to be a lie. If pressed further, the Daradeen will not reveal the location of the future regent.

entries.title: The Ransacked Residence
entries: The Daradeen Ambassador's residence is in the habitat ring of Gymir station. Reaching this area requires travel up to the central hub and then back down one of the structural spokes. A passkey is required to enter the ring level on which the residence is located.

A successful {@difficulty hard|Computers} or {@difficulty average|Skulduggery} utilizing a {@gear punch card machine} will bypass security. Alternately, a {@difficulty hard|Mechanics} can brute force the security locks.

This level is gorgeously appointed, with beds of exotic plantings, fountains, and ponds full of colorful fish. Faux clouds pattern the lighting arrays overhead. Balconies and suspended walkways overlook the lower residence levels and an artificial stream a hundred meters below.

Whether the PCs arrive at the Ambassador's residence on their own or with the Daradeens, they find the large doorway to the suite open and unattended. The security systems have been deactivated, and a guard lies unconscious just inside the entrance.

The guard can be roused with a successful {@difficulty average|Medicine}. They say that they were surprised and overwhelmed by several attackers. The guard describes a man that the PCs recognize as {@adversary Yortin Fleinn}.

A search determines that the Sapphire Lily is missing. If the PCs are alone, a successful {@difficulty average|Perception} finds 2k in precious gems and a safe. A successful {@difficulty hard|Skulduggery} will open the safe, which contains 4k Sols in hard currency. All this should indicate that the thieves were only after the Sapphire Lily.

A successful {@difficulty hard|Computers} will give the PCs access to the scanner logs and the physical characteristics of the thieves. One is undeniably Yortin Fleinn. A muddled audio recording gives a clue: the phrase Caves of Disin. A successful {@difficulty average|Knowledge} allows the PC to recognize the name as referring to the asteroid caves on one of Aegir's larger moonlets, Blar Kirkja.

If present, the Daradeens will offer the PCs a reward of 10k Sols if they are able to retrieve the Sapphire Lily. Anju will also insist on accompanying the PCs. Ambassador Sudh and Representative Gnanik at first argue against the idea, but Anju quickly reminds them of the importance of the Lily, and they relent.

If the PCs do not want Anju to accompany them, the reward is increased to 13k Sols if they acquiesce. If not enough, Anju will attempt an Opposed {@skill Charm} check, or begin a social encounter, to convince the PCs. They are willing to pay up to 15k Sols in the end.

entries.title: Who is Anju?
entries: At this point the PCs may suspect that young {@adversary Anju} is more than just an attaché. If pressed with a successful {@difficulty hard|Charm}, they will admit to being a member of the Royal Court, and therefore of higher rank than both the ambassador and Representative Gnanik.

The truth is that Anju is the future Regent, and they will return to claim the throne of Daradeen once they have found a foreign 'noble' to marry. What constitutes a 'noble' is unclear even to Anju, but they intend to choose their own spouse. The return of the Sapphire Lily is the only way to assure that outcome.
The PCs may discover Anju's true identity when the GM thinks best, preferably at a dramatic moment.

While accompanying the PCs, Anju can prove useful by upgrading important rolls with their {@adversaryAbility Born Leader} ability. They can also serve as the voice of the GM, helping to spur the PCs on toward recovering the Sapphire Lily.

entries.title: Well, Well, Well
entries: Just after the PCs exit the Ambassador's residence, they hear a chime indicating an artificial rainstorm is about to begin. They have time to reach the lifts, needing only to cross the suspended walkway leading to the lift lobby.
Here they are accosted by several of Morgessa's {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs}. Read or paraphrase the following:
Three well-muscled, rough looking people block the walkway ahead. Their ship suits are familiar, marking them as more of Morgessa's {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs}.
'Morgessa was right, you are involved with that rat Fleinn! Hand over the jewel, or you all are going to see how rats are dealt with in Vordun!'
There is the hum of a pair of Knucklers powering on from behind you, as two more {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} appear from around a fountain.

They are demanding the Sapphire Lily, convinced the PCs are in league with Fleinn. This will likely start a combat encounter. The {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} are not pulling punches, and one or more immediately inject themselves with {@adversaryAbility Metamorphic Serum}. They will kill the PCs if they can.

The walkway is narrow enough to create a bottleneck, and the {@adversary Vordun Thug|thugs} may try to push the PCs over the edge, triggering a {@rule falling|fall} at short range to another walkway below.
After the first round of combat, another chime sounds from overhead, and an artificial rainstorm begins. This adds {@dice setback} to all skill checks, and {@dice setback|2} to combat checks.

entries.title: Tracking Fleinn
entries: If the PCs have not discovered that {@adversary Yortin Fleinn} has the Lily, a successful {@difficulty easy|Perception} finds a silver brooch in the lift lobby or on the walkway which the PCs recognize as belonging to Fleinn. The PCs might also receive a {@gear hand radio} call from Sharan Joels the intelligence agent that puts them on Fleinn's trail, or a call from Fleinn himself offering to sell the Sapphire Lily. If the latter, then Fleinn tells the PCs to meet him on Blar Kirkja, a moonlet with extensive natural caves.

There is a security terminal in the lift lobby, and others throughout the station. A successful {@difficulty average|Computers} at one can search the station's logs for Yortin Fleinn's name and find that he has requested clearance for a shuttle departure. Alternately, a successful {@difficulty average|Streetwise} in the commercial section of the station finds someone who overheard Fleinn talking about 'going to ground' for a few days until something blows over. A successful {@difficulty average|Knowledge} can reveal that the many moonlets orbiting Aegir often serve as hiding places for smugglers and thieves.

If the PCs are not able to pick up Fleinn's trail, they can spot him entering a lift to the docking spires. Pursuing him will lead them to a shuttle bay just as he is departing the station. As a reminder, the spires and station center are a {@rule Gravity|micro-gravity environment}.

chapters.title: Section 2: Blar Kirkja
entries: Blar Kirkja is an irregular moonlet that spans fifty kilometers at its widest point. Extensive caves and mine shafts wind beneath the grey rock and dust of the planetesimal's surface. One of the first bodies around Aegir to be mined, Blar Kirkja was treated with an almost superstitious reverence in the early days of Epsilon Eridani's settlement, but that time was centuries ago.

entries.title: Quiet, and Dark
entries: An old mining dock is the only facility with power readings on Blar Kirkja. Tall cliffs surround the space dock, requiring a successful {@rule Dangerous Driving} check to dock with one of the two passive docking ports that are still active. The other port is occupied by another {@vehicle Saucer-class Shuttle|saucer shuttle} craft. As the shuttle docks, the characters feel the light gravity of the moonlet take hold.

The PCs' saucer has {@gear Space Suit|spacesuits} for the party, which will be required to enter the facility as it is no longer pressurized. A successful {@difficulty average|Mechanics or Skulduggery} is needed to open the secured docking hatch.

Once inside, the PCs find a cavernous, empty cargo bay. The meager lamps provided with the spacesuits barely illuminate the cart rails that lead into two large tunnels cut into the rock wall opposite the dock. A control station, stripped of its parts, overlooks the room from atop a raised platform.

If the PCs wish to investigate the other shuttle, a successful {@difficulty hard|Mechanics or Skulduggery} opens the docking hatch. Success on an {@difficulty average|Computers} confirms that this was {@adversary Yortin Fleinn}'s shuttle.
A successful {@difficulty easy|Perception or Survival} spots fresh tracks through the dust on the cargo bay's floor. {@symbols a} can reveal any of the following:

items: A symbol that marks the same passage to which the tracks lead.
There is evidence of other recent visitors to this facility.
It seems that people regularly use this dock every few weeks.

entries: A successful {@difficulty average|Knowledge}, or {@symbols a} generated on the check, can reveal any of the following about the symbol:

items: The marking is the name Disa, written in an old runic language.
The rune is written in a manner that indicates a direction, like a trail marker.
There were once religious cults in the Epsilon Eridani system that used this ancient language.
Disa is the name of a mythological woman associated with sacrifice.

entries.title: A Forgotten Place
entries: One of the tunnels leads into the housing section of the facility and is ultimately a dead end. Again, anything of use has been stripped, and the old mess hall, infirmary, entertainment room, and crew quarters are eerie in the airless dark. A successful {@difficulty average|Perception} discovers an old, but serviceable, {@gear Medical Case|medicine case} and four {@gear Palliative Tonic|palliative tonics}.

The other tunnel, where the tracks from the cargo bay lead, opens into an ore processing center. Huge conveyor belts and giant bins and chutes are all that remains of the machinery here. Beyond this begin the mining tunnels leading deeper into the rock.

In the ore processing center the PCs encounter an {@adversary Old Mining Robot|old mining robot}. A successful out-of-turn {@difficulty hard|Vigilance} will spot the robot before it activates. A successful {@difficulty hard|Stealth} is required to approach the robot without triggering its defenses. A successful {@difficulty hard|Mechanics} can disable the robot. Otherwise, the large machine activates and attacks the PCs.
Read or paraphrase the following:

A cloud of dust accompanies the vibrations through the rock beneath your feet, as the ancient robot unfolds itself. Kaleidoscopic blinking lights illuminate the mist of particles that rain down around you, while the machine's large manipulator arms cut deep furrows of shadow through the glow.
The robot focuses its receptors on your group. One sturdy leg swings forward as it attacks.

{@symbols hhh} generated on any check during the encounter can loosen an air hose on that character's spacesuit, causing the loss of fifteen minutes of breathable air before they can reattach the hose.

During the encounter, it is recommended to use the {@rule Nemesis Extra Activation Rules|additional activation optional rule} for the robot. On this activation, the robot can use their {@adversaryAbility Stomp} ability to shake the machinery and rock walls with its heavy footfalls, triggering an out-of-turn {@difficulty hard|Coordination} for each of the PCs. Failure knocks the character {@rule prone}, while each {@symbols h} generated causes one wound.

Success on an {@difficulty average|Perception} in the ore processing center finds an emergency kit with two {@gear Palliative Tonic|palliative tonics} and three {@gear Adrenaline Hypo|adrenaline hypos}.

entries.title: Deeper, One Must Go
entries: Quickly finding their way through the tunnels requires the PCs to succeed on an {@difficulty average|Survival}, with an upgrade if they previously discovered the recent tracks through the dust. This takes one hour, minus fifteen minutes per {@symbols a} after the first. Failure means the PCs become lost in the tunnels and luckily reach the final chamber with only a few minutes of oxygen left in their suits. {@symbols a} can be used to find the following:

items: More of the glyphs mark the cave walls, and clearly indicate a path through the tunnels.
The recent tracks follow the path indicated by the symbols.
A spacesuit lies crumpled along a passage, containing a desiccated body and a half-full oxygen tank with an hour of breathable air.

entries: As the PCs reach the end of the maze of tunnels, they encounter an airlock set into a stone wall. A successful {@difficulty average|Computers} can access the airlock's closed circuit camera, giving a view of more tunnel beyond. A successful {@difficulty hard|Mechanics or Skulduggery} can cycle the airlock and allow the PCs to pass through.
Once through the airlock, a hand scanner can verify the presence of breathable atmosphere. The PCs spacesuits will automatically recharge their tanks.

The characters are now in a natural tunnel, unworked and jagged with rocky projections. Ahead, there is the glow of artificial light. A large glyph is painted on the wall here, and success on an {@difficulty average|Knowledge} translates the word as Disablot. {@symbols a} can reveal the following:

items: Disablot is the name of an ancient ritual, meaning blood sacrifice.
There are rumors that some who seek refuge among the asteroids orbiting the gas giant Aegir disappear without a trace.

entries.title: Just What Has Been Found?
entries: A successful {@difficulty easy|Perception} will note the sounds of voices echoing down the tunnel from up ahead. {@symbols a} can be used to make out one of the voices – that of {@adversary Yortin Fleinn} – pleading for his life.

As the PCs make their way along the natural tunnel, the passage grows wider. A slab of smooth stone overhead, tilted at an angle and running for ten meters, is painted with a mural of pictures and glyphs. A successful {@difficulty easy|Knowledge} deciphers the story of a woman, Disa, saving the lives of hundreds of innocents by choosing just a few people to be sacrificed instead.

The tunnel opens into a large, cathedral-like space lit by the glow of flood lights angled up toward the craggy ceiling above. The far walls of the space are folded and uneven, creating deep pools of shadow. In the center of the space (long range to the PCs) a dozen people, wrapped in tight garments made of fur, stand in a loose circle around an altar of black stone. A man has been laid upon the altar, bound by hand and foot. It is Yortin Fleinn.
Read or paraphrase the following:
A group of a dozen figures, clad in furs and swaying to a slow chant they intone in unison, are arrayed around a jet black altar of stone.

One figure stands beside the altar, her tight hood of white fur thrown back to reveal silver hair and a severe, lined face. In her hands she holds a transparent case, inside of which is a large jewel, intricately carved into the shape of a flower.
'Please, Gertra, I will give you the Lily if you let me free!' Fleinn's tone is desperate.
'That jewel has value beyond its beauty alone. Whoever holds it will wield great power, as the Regent of Daradeen must marry the one who presents it!'
The silver haired woman looks down at Fleinn with a stern and unforgiving expression.
'I know exactly what I hold, Yortin. With this blessing the Followers of Disa will at last move from the darkness into the light. A shame you will not see it.'
'Begin the sacrifice.'

At {@adversary Gertra|Gertra's} words two of the other figures move toward the altar, both drawing forth long blades that shine in the reflected flood lights. Gertra strides toward the back of the chamber while the volume of the chanting increases. If uninterrupted, the cultists end Fleinn's life.

The PCs may want to begin an encounter with the {@adversary Follower of Disa|Followers of Disa}, or they might try to pursue Gertra without interfering with the ritual. Success on a {@difficulty hard|Stealth} will allow the PCs to circle the edge of the chamber without alerting the cultists. As they do, Gertra has exited the room via a passage concealed in the shadows of the far wall.
If the cultists become aware of the PCs they will attack them as Gertra leaves through the concealed passage, forming three minion groups of four each.

Once the PCs do follow Gertra, they find a narrow natural tunnel through the stone that at times becomes difficult to pass through. A successful {@difficulty average|Coordination} is required to pass without injury. A failed check deals one wound per uncanceled {@symbols f} and one strain per uncanceled {@symbols h}, ignoring soak. While this happens the sound of a cycling airlock echoes down the passage from up ahead.

When the PCs reach the airlock it should be obvious from the readouts that there is no breathable air on the other side. Arrayed along the wall near the airlock are a dozen {@gear Space Suit|space suits}.

No check is needed to cycle through the airlock, and when the PCs do, they find a large cavern that has been converted to a landing bay for several saucer shuttles. Across the space is a rift in the stone that provides a breathtaking view of the gas giant Aegir against a sea of stars.

Long range to the PCs, between the airlock and the five saucers, are twelve people in spacesuits involved in a confrontation. Once again, the PCs recognize the colors and insignia of {@adversary Morgessa|Morgessa's} crew, as she and six of her henchmen block Gertra and five of her followers from approaching the shuttles. Everyone involved has weapons drawn, save Gertra who has a bulky duffle bag over her shoulder.
Anyone with a {@gear hand radio} can find the frequency that the two groups are using to communicate. If they do, read or paraphrase the following:
'Listen you old loony, that jewel belongs to the Despot of Vordun, and I intend to bring it to him,' says Morgessa in an exasperated voice.
'Nonsense, this is a gift from our mistress, Disa. I will be married to the Regent of Daradeen and use that mighty fleet to bring Disa's truth to the galaxy. Out of our way!'
'You're going nowhere, fruitcake. Hand over the Sapphire Lily and I will let you live.'
Gertra laughs, declaring, 'I will do you no such favor, witch! Kill her!'

The two groups attack one another. If the PCs have not heard the above conversation, they simply watch a fight break out between the two groups. If they do not interfere, two members of each group fall to the first volley of weapons fire. Soon, however, Morgessa's gang takes the upper hand. As Gertra's last follower drops, she holds up a hand and then tosses her duffle toward Morgessa. The gang leader strides forward toward the duffle bag and Gertra backs away.

Morgessa snatches up the duffle and rips it open, pulling forth an empty transparent box. Before she has time to react Gertra scrambles up the ramp into one of the saucer shuttles and manages to take off. Morgessa's gang is not able to stop her.

If the PCs choose to involve themselves in the confrontation, a confusing, three-way encounter ensues. Gertra will attempt to escape with the Sapphire Lily stuffed inside her {@gear space suit}. The cult leader will toss the duffle toward Morgessa as a distraction, and during a heavy firefight the gang leader will not spare the time to check the duffle bag as she grabs it.
Anju, if they are present, begs the PCs to be careful not to damage the Sapphire Lily.

Any of the adversaries might fire into the ceiling above the PCs during the encounter, causing a rock fall. A successful {@difficulty average|Coordination or Athletics} is required to avoid being knocked {@rule prone}, with each uncanceled {@symbols f} causing one wound ignoring soak.

{@symbols hhh} or a despair generated on any PC skill check can result in a tear in that character's {@gear space suit}. A successful {@difficulty easy|Mechanics} is required to repair the damage. Otherwise, all breathable atmosphere escapes the suit in three rounds.

Should the PCs manage to incapacitate Gertra, one of her followers performs the distraction with the duffle bag and drags the cult leader onto the shuttle. If the PCs prevent this outcome another of the cultists manages to escape, having had the Sapphire Lily all along. If necessary, they have been faking their death since early in the encounter.
Morgessa, for her part, will use her {@b {@adversaryAbility Live to Fight Again}} ability to escape, should she be reduced to half her wound threshold.

entries.title: Follow That Shuttle!
entries: The PCs can easily board any of the remaining {@vehicle Saucer-class Shuttle|saucer-class shuttles}. A {@rule Dangerous Driving} check is needed to safely exit the ersatz landing bay.

Success on an {@difficulty easy|Computers} will track the other shuttle crafts that have just left the cavern. Alternately, a successful {@difficulty average|Perception} will spot the other shuttle through the viewport. If needed, Anju or a crackling communication from Agent Sharan Joels can point the PCs toward Gertra's goal.
Gertra, or her follower, is headed toward a Daradeen ship that floats alone in an orbit two kilometers from Gymir station.

Anju, if they are present, identifies the ship as the Khojakarta. This is the ship that they and Representative Gnanik arrived on, which is tasked with delivering the Sapphire Lily to an appropriate spouse for the new regent-to-be. If the PCs do not yet know, Anju informs them that the future regent will marry whoever presents them the Sapphire Lily.
The saucer-class shuttle that carries Gertra or her follower docks with the Khojakarta. No check is needed for the PCs to also dock with the {@vehicle Chaandanee-class Sloop|Chaandanee-class sloop}.

chapters.title: Section 3: The Khojakarta
entries: A prototype Daradeen vessel, the Khojakarta is as gorgeous to behold as it is deadly. Sleek, bristling with weapons ports, and obviously newly built, this {@vehicle Chaandanee-class Sloop|Chaandanee-class sloop} hangs in orbit around Aegir, glinting against the blackness of space.

entries.title: A Gift or a Curse
entries: As the PCs exit the shuttle, they see Gertra (or her follower) floating in the center of the docking bay facing a half circle of Daradeen crew-people. The PCs also recognize Agent {@adversary Sharan Joels} who is for some reason among the Daradeen. If {@adversary Anju} did not accompany the PCs earlier, they are also present.
As a reminder, ships not under way are a {@rule Gravity|micro-gravity environment}, which adds {@dice setback|2} to all {@characteristic Brawn} and {@characteristic Agility} checks.
Read or paraphrase the following:
The Cultist of Disa floats in the center of the docking bay before a half circle of Daradeen, the Sapphire Lily held above her head.
'Bring the new regent to me, immediately! I am their rightful betrothed, as I possess the Sapphire…'
A beam of energy pierces the woman's chest, silencing the cultist as the Sapphire Lily twirls from her hand. Agent Sharan Joels lowers her weapon, a cold smile painted across her lips.
'Thank you, Sharan,' says Morgessa, who is framed by one of the airlocks that ring the docking bay, her burner drawn.
'Keep your soldiers back, Regent Anju,' Agent Joels says with a sneer. 'No Daradeen can interfere with this conflict.'
Anju looks at you with sadness in her eyes, confirming, 'It is true, by custom I cannot stop this fight for the Sapphire Lily, and for my hand in marriage.'

{@adversary Morgessa} launches herself toward the Sapphire Lily, starting the final structured encounter of the adventure. If she manages to capture the jewel, she and Sharan Joels will attempt to flee by returning to her {@vehicle Saucer-class Shuttle|saucer-class shuttle}. The two women will fight to the death to achieve this goal, and if Morgessa is {@rule incapacitated} Sharan will try to flee alone with the Sapphire Lily.

Morgessa cannot use her {@b {@adversaryAbility Live to Fight Again}} ability in this encounter, though she may resort to injecting herself with {@adversaryAbility Metamorphic Serum|metamorphic serum} if reduced to half her Wound or Strain threshold.

entries.title: What Future May Come
entries: If Morgessa or Sharan Joels succeed in escaping with the Sapphire Lily their last words are as follows:
'Soon the Despot of Vordun will find you, Regent Anju, and claim his place by your side as your rightful husband!'
If the PCs recover the Sapphire Lily, they are paid a reward of 15k Sols by Regent-to-be Anju, no matter what they negotiated earlier.

If one of the characters presents the intricately carved jewel to Anju, either on purpose or by accident, they are now betrothed in the eyes of the Daradeen and destined to rule by Anju's side. Anju's presence almost instantly becomes intoxicating to the PC that presents the Sapphire Lily, as the Daradeen's fluid identity comports to their future spouse. The Regent-to-be has their own free will, and while the strict, almost mystical nature of Daradeen tradition requires a marriage, Anju does not have to be happy about it. A betrothed PC is likely to find that they are subject to rituals and social pressure that they do not enjoy.

Finally, should the GM desire a cliffhanger for the end of the adventure, sirens blare throughout the Khojakarta, calling the crew to battle stations. Morgessa's {@vehicle Ca Den Raider-class Frigate|Ca Den Raider} has attacked the Daradeen Sloop, seeking to avenge her death!
